items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Med Flory plays two choruses, Lanny Morgan plays two choruses

ctx.x: And colleges are buying them left and right. I was just doing a clinic and a few of the college people said, “Are you kidding, we ordered fourteen.” Because they don’t write arrangements like that anymore. They’re just straight ahead swing music. And especially if you want to show the band off, if you play the arrangements like it’s really written, because I actually patterned the band after the Benny Goodman band because Benny played in and out. Because it didn’t blend with the section. It did, but it would…

items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I was working a lot with the new Terry Gibbs band

ctx.x: The Ferguson band seemed to be one of the hottest things going. That was 13 pieces? Thirteen, 14?

Thirteen pieces. Well I think it was. I may be a little prejudiced. I think at times during that particular band’s lifetime, which was probably 1957 through when he left New York which was early ’66, I think that band was maybe four, five times — nobody could touch it. It was the hottest band in the world, and I’m including everybody. Actually I played with that band in 1957 before I went in the service. Willie Maiden was an old friend of mine. And he was playing baritone on the band and he got sick one night,…
